meta.note: Rocks & minerals reference layer: curated rock types and silica varieties (agate, chalcedony, chert, petrified wood, concretions, geodes) with localities, plus Wikidata mineral properties (Mohs hardness, crystal system, color, streak). Facts and links only.

types.name: Agate (banded chalcedony), incl. plume and tube agate
types.region_notes: Graveyard Point, Owyhee County, Idaho / Malheur County, Oregon (seam/plume agate); Nevada; Texas: Big Bend (Woodward Ranch)
localities: Graveyard Point, Owyhee County, Idaho / Malheur County, Oregon (seam/plume agate)
types.diagnostic: Chalcedony in concentric or parallel bands; plume agate holds feathery inclusions; tube agate shows straw-like tubes formed around mineral fibers. Graveyard Point (Idaho-Oregon border) is a classic plume/seam agate locality in Miocene volcanic rocks.

types.name: Calcite
types.diagnostic: Soft (knife scratches it), fizzes in acid, breaks into rhombs.

types.name: Chalcedony
types.diagnostic: Translucent, waxy microfibrous quartz, often filling cavities; banded varieties are agate.

types.name: Chert / flint
types.region_notes: Edwards Plateau, TX; Colorado River gravels, TX; Chalk of England/France
types.diagnostic: Microcrystalline quartz rock that breaks with smooth conchoidal fractures and sharp edges; nodules often have a chalky cortex. The main stone for Texas tools.

types.name: Concretion / septarian nodule / iron concretion
types.diagnostic: A hard mass of cemented sediment that grew around a nucleus; septarian nodules have crack networks filled with calcite.

types.name: Granite / granitic rocks
types.diagnostic: Coarse interlocking crystals of feldspar, quartz and mica.

types.name: Gypsum / selenite
types.diagnostic: Very soft (fingernail scratches it); selenite is clear platy crystals, satin spar is fibrous.

types.name: Ironstone / iron-oxide rind (goethite, hematite, limonite)
types.diagnostic: Iron oxides coat or cement rocks; the streak test (brown/red) separates them from stained chert.

types.name: Lignite / jet
types.diagnostic: Soft, lightweight brown-black coal; may show woody texture. Mined from the Wilcox near Bastrop.

types.name: Limestone / chalk
types.diagnostic: Calcium carbonate rock; fizzes in dilute acid; often fossil-rich. Chalk is soft, white, fine limestone.

types.name: Natural water-worn pebble or cobble
types.diagnostic: Rounded by water transport; no flake scars, pecking or ground facets.

types.name: Petrified wood (silicified/agatized/opalized)
types.region_notes: Catahoula Fm, Texas (state stone); Virgin Valley & Hubbard Basin, Nevada; Petrified Forest, Arizona
types.diagnostic: Wood replaced by chalcedony/quartz or opal, keeping grain and rings. Nevada (Virgin Valley, Hubbard Basin, Fallon area) is known for Miocene wood. Texas made petrified palmwood its state stone.

types.name: Pyrite / marcasite nodules
types.diagnostic: Brassy metallic, greenish-black streak; marcasite nodules have radiating interiors.

types.name: Quartz (vein, rose, crystal)
types.diagnostic: Glassy, hard (scratches glass), no cleavage; drusy quartz is a crust of tiny crystals lining cavities.

types.name: Quartzite
types.diagnostic: Quartz sandstone so tightly cemented or metamorphosed that it breaks through the grains; sugary sparkle.

types.name: Sandstone
types.diagnostic: Sand-sized grains cemented together; grains rub off and the rock breaks around grains.

types.name: Silicified limestone
types.diagnostic: Limestone partly replaced by silica: hard and does not fizz where silicified, often preserving fossils in chert.

types.name: Common opal
types.diagnostic: Hydrated amorphous silica, slightly softer and lighter than chalcedony; may replace wood.

types.name: Geode / thunder egg
types.region_notes: Oregon & Idaho (thunder eggs); Midwest US geodes
types.diagnostic: Rounded rock with a hollow interior lined with crystals (quartz, calcite); thunder eggs are filled with agate.

types.name: Volcanic rocks (basalt, rhyolite, tuff)
types.region_notes: Owyhee volcanics (Idaho/Oregon); Nevada; Big Bend, Texas
types.diagnostic: Rocks from lava or ash; vesicles (gas holes) are common. Hosts the agate of Graveyard Point and Nevada.
